newsitem.title: MONGOLIA: Mongolia holds first land auction.
newsitem.headline: Mongolia holds first land auction.

text.p: Mongolia has held its first land auction, selling off three small sites in the nation's capital, the official Auction Commission said on Monday.
The plots fetched prices of 19 million to 33.3 million tugriks ($23,947 to $41,970), or $108.85 to $234.05 per square metre, the commission said.
The three sites, ranging from 140 to 240 square metres (1,500 to 2,580 square feet), were designated for commercial use and would most likely be used for small shops.
All three buyers of the sites in suburban districts of Ulan Bator were local companies. Amno Company, a trading and garment firm, purchased the largest site at auction on Friday.
The commission said other sites would be auctioned in future though it gave no details.
Natsagiin Bagabandi, candidate of the former communist party, upset reformist President Punsalmaagiin Ochirbat in presidential elections two weeks ago.
Some Western diplomats have expressed concern that the new president, to be inaugurated on June 20, might slow the pace of Mongolia's market style reforms, particularly its plans for privatisation.
